correctness.rationale: Equation (1) is the exact fixed-full-isolation single-resource source model. Equations (2)–(4) follow from monotone mass balance. The exact relative-entropy identity (8) is verified algebraically, with every transfer term bounded by two sharp AM–GM inequalities and all missing-species invasion terms nonpositive. Its compact sublevels and invariant zero-dissipation set prove all-positive-orbit global convergence even at species-loss boundaries. Distinct break-even values give a simple critical eigenvalue; the complementary dynamics are Hurwitz. Equations (10)–(11) derive the strictly positive center coefficient and hence the universal biomass and nutrient \(1/\tau\) amplitudes. check.py passed exact symbolic identities, rational equilibrium conditions and numerical illustrations; infinite-time claims follow from the proof, not finite computation.

originality.rationale: The full initiating 2026 primary source establishes a two-species stationary coexistence condition but not the universal critical \(\tau^{-1}\) extinction coefficient or boundary global convergence for arbitrary distinct break-even levels. Previously accessible equilibrium-support/local-hyperbolic theorems and interior-global-stability statements leave those neutral boundary regimes untreated. Searches for resource-competition aliases, chemostat extinction, full local isolation and center-manifold asymptotics uncovered no exact theorem. The major older chemostat and patch-diffusion sources use different equations or positive-state assumptions. Historical priority remains bounded by the accessible material, not asserted as a definitive uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: Complete article bodies of some older diffusion chemostat papers, notably the 2019 two-patch and 2023 source-sink works, could not be inspected; their different stated state-space structures reduce but do not eliminate priority risk.
The accessible 2012 and 2016 general-chemostat records were not sufficient for full theorem-by-theorem comparison, although the claimed assumptions and aims differ.
An older unindexed neutral-invasion chemostat theorem or unpublished reduction might contain an equivalent local rate law.
Global convergence only covers strictly positive initial biomass, with all break-even levels distinct, and no stochastic forcing.

value.rationale: The ecology paper motivates survivor richness changes with nutrient-exchange rate, but steady-state predictions cannot distinguish rapid disappearance from critical persistent traces. The exact ordered thresholds, global outcome selection from any strictly positive initial community and universal critical biomass/nutrient \(1/\tau\) coefficients identify a concrete ecological bottleneck that matters for finite-horizon inference and numerical extinction detection. The coefficients are natural observables tied to resource uptake and the resident community, not an arbitrarily chosen parameter slice. No general theorem or experiment is claimed beyond the defined deterministic model.
